name: Graphite
tagline: Ink on white. Colour only where the data is.
jobs: Analytics apps, internal apps and tools

tokens.name: canvas
tokens.usage: Page ground: plain white by day, near-black by night. Content sits directly on it.

tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: Cards, fields, menus, dialogs. The same white as the page by day, so a card is drawn by its hairline alone.

tokens.name: sunk
tokens.usage: The side rail, table headers, code wells, a tip at the foot of a page: the one ground a step off white.

tokens.name: tint
tokens.usage: Hover, the selected nav item, secondary buttons and the small selects inside a pill.

tokens.name: hairline
tokens.usage: Every border and divider, and chart gridlines (dashed). One weight, everywhere.

tokens.name: hairline-strong
tokens.usage: Field borders, the zero line of a chart, borders on hover.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Text, icons and the primary fill: the filled button is ink, not a colour.

tokens.name: ink-soft
tokens.usage: Secondary text: labels, timestamps, helper text, axis labels, group headings in the rail.

tokens.name: ink-faint
tokens.usage: Tertiary text and the drawing line: placeholders, disabled labels, hints.

tokens.name: on-ink
tokens.usage: Text and icons on an ink fill.

tokens.name: mark
tokens.usage: A mark, never a fill: the focus ring, the running dot, a selected chart-type icon, one glyph of a logo. Never a button, surface or body text.

tokens.name: positive
tokens.usage: Success text and dots, the up-delta. Always beside a word.

tokens.name: positive-soft
tokens.usage: Ground for success tags.

tokens.name: caution
tokens.usage: Warnings and pending states.

tokens.name: caution-soft
tokens.usage: Ground for warning tags and notes.

tokens.name: negative
tokens.usage: Errors, destructive actions, the down-delta.

tokens.name: negative-soft
tokens.usage: Ground for error tags and callouts.

tokens.name: turquoise
tokens.usage: First chart series; the date-column mark. Data only.

tokens.name: river
tokens.usage: Second chart series; the number-column mark. Data only.

tokens.name: alizarin
tokens.usage: Third chart series. Data only; status red is negative.

tokens.name: amethyst
tokens.usage: Fourth chart series. Data only.

tokens.name: carrot
tokens.usage: Fifth chart series; the mark of a string column. Data only.

tokens.name: asphalt
tokens.usage: Sixth chart series, for "other": wet asphalt by day, concrete by night.

tokens.name: sunflower
tokens.usage: Seventh chart series. Data only; never text on white.

tokens.name: emerald
tokens.usage: Eighth chart series, kept last: beside turquoise the two blur.

type_roles.name: display-xl
type_roles.usage: One per page, for a landing hero. Semibold with tight tracking; Graphite never goes bold.

type_roles.name: display-m
type_roles.usage: The one greeting or page heading that opens a screen.

type_roles.name: title
type_roles.usage: Card titles, dialog titles, list heads. The page name in a top bar.

type_roles.name: body-l
type_roles.sample: Charts read best when the chrome around them says nothing at all.
type_roles.usage: Lead paragraphs and the question box.

type_roles.name: body
type_roles.sample: Each query runs as you, under the active group, so you only see what you may.
type_roles.usage: Default UI and reading text: 14px at 1.5.

type_roles.name: body-s
type_roles.usage: Captions, helper text, dense cells, timestamps.

type_roles.name: label
type_roles.usage: Field labels, shelf labels, column heads. Medium weight, sentence case, no tracking.

type_roles.name: eyebrow
type_roles.usage: Group headings in a rail or above a list: the soft ink at 12px, sentence case. Graphite has no caps and no letter-spacing.

type_roles.name: numeral
type_roles.usage: KPI figures, tabular, in the sans.

type_roles.name: mono
type_roles.usage: SQL, code, IDs, paths. Nowhere else.

idea_headline: Grey and ink, so the data is the colour.
idea: Graphite is the look of an analytics tool that keeps its own voice down: a white page, a light grey rail, hairline borders and near-black ink. The filled button is ink, not a brand colour; selection is a grey pill. Colour appears in exactly two places, the data (flat, vivid series on a dashed grid) and small marks (a kind icon, a status dot, the focus ring), so the first coloured thing anyone sees is an answer.
use_for: Analytics and BI apps, data exploration and query tools, internal admin tools, run and job monitors, settings and access screens, and any product where charts and tables are the content.
avoid_when: Editorial or narrative subjects, consumer brands with a colour to show, warm or textured subjects, or a marketing page that needs a loud brand moment.
principles: Actions, selection and navigation are grey and ink. Colour is reserved for series, column kinds and status, so it always means data or state, never "click here".
No shadows on anything that sits on the page: a card is a hairline on white. Only menus, dialogs and popovers float, with one soft shadow.
The page and its cards are the same white; the rail and table headers are one step of grey. Two grounds are enough.
Dashed hairline grids both ways, a solid zero, no axis lines, compact labels, softened fills and a legend underneath. The data sits forward; the scaffolding recedes.
Instrument Sans at 14px with 1.5 leading for everything readable; semibold with tight tracking for headings. No caps, no letter-spacing, no bold.
voice: Plain and literal: "Run a query to see rows." "No rows match. Loosen a filter."
Sentence case everywhere, including buttons, shelf labels and column heads.
Say what happened and what to do next; an error names the reason, never apologises.
Name things by what people see: "Open in SQL", not "View compiled statement".
colour_headline: White, one grey, ink, and the data.
colour_note: Day is a white page with a light grey rail; Night is near-black with cards one step lighter. The hairline is the only structural colour. Ink is the action colour. The mark (a deep teal) is a mark only: the focus ring, the running dot, a selected icon. Status colours always come with a word. The chart series are a flat palette used for data alone.
chart_note: Flat, equally vivid hues, ordered so neighbours differ most: turquoise, river blue, alizarin, amethyst, carrot, then asphalt for "other". Emerald is last because it blurs into turquoise. Gridlines are the dashed hairline; zero is solid; fills are softened (bars 82%, areas 38%).
type_note: One family for headings and UI: 400 for reading, 500 for labels and buttons, 600 for headings and titles with tracking that tightens as size grows. JetBrains Mono is for SQL, code and IDs only. Numbers in tables and stats are tabular.
space_headline: A 4px step, an 8px corner, a 1px line.
space: Icon to label; inside a pill.
Between pills; inside controls; between stacked fields.
Card gaps in dense views; table cell padding-x.
Card padding; gap between cards and boards.
Page padding inside the main column.
Above a page-closing tip or footer.
The top of a greeting page: the question sits low, in its own air.
edges: Small selects inside a pill, keyboard keys, nav items in a dense rail.
Buttons, fields, pills, menus. The default.
Cards, boards, dialogs, the question box.
Every border, every divider, dashed for chart grids and empty adders.
depth: Everything on the page is flat: a hairline on white, no shadow, no highlight.
Menus, dialogs, popovers and toasts: a 1px contact shadow and one soft 32px drop. The only shadow.
The selected item in a segmented control or mode rail is a white tile with the faintest contact shadow on the grey track.
A 2px gap then 2px of the mark colour, on every control.
motion: Surfaces tint one grey step in 120ms. Nothing moves.
No scale, no bounce; the hover tint holds.
None by default. A chart redraws in place; a running query dims the old result to 55% until the new one lands.
One: the running dot pulses in the mark colour every 1.2s.
No entry animation: the answer appears. Reduced motion changes nothing.
components_headline: The kit, in grey and ink.
components_note: Graphite maps the kit's primary to ink and its secondary and accent to the grey tint, so kit components arrive monochrome: ink buttons, grey selection, hairline fields. Charts take the flat series in order.
buttons: <Button>Save result</Button><Button variant="secondary">Duplicate</Button><Button variant="outline">Set up your agent</Button><Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button><button className="gr-btn gr-btn-primary">Ask <kbd className="gr-kbd gr-kbd-on">↵</kbd></button><button className="gr-btn">Save result</button><button className="gr-btn gr-btn-ghost">Open in SQL</button><button className="gr-btn gr-btn-danger">Remove filter</button>
buttons_note: Kit buttons left; authored gr-btn right. The primary is an ink fill with white text, inverted at night, and fades slightly on hover; the secondary is white with the strong hairline; the ghost is bare text that takes the tint on hover. Danger is red text until hovered.
tags: AdminModelDraftRefusedSucceededQueuedFailedDraftRunning
tags_note: A tag is a dot and a word on a soft ground, sentence case. Running is ink text with a pulsing mark-colour dot; every other state holds still.
fields_note: Fields are white with the strong hairline, the label above in the label role (13px medium, sentence case). Focus adds the mark-colour ring; the border stays.
stats:
Revenue↑ 12.4% vs last month
Orders+84 this month
stats_note: A stat is a label, a sans numeral and a delta, sharing one card split by hairlines. Only the delta takes colour, and only with an arrow and a word.
callouts:
Query refusedYour group may not read finance.ledger. An administrator grants access in Data policy.
Runs as you. Every query uses your group's policy; nothing is unrestricted by default.
Saved. The result is in Artifacts as Revenue by region.
No rows match. Loosen a filter to see data.
callouts_note: A callout is a quiet grey box with a bold lead-in; success and error swap the ground for their soft colour. No left rules, no icons needed.
chart_comp_note: Charts take turquoise first and river second. Dashed hairline grids both ways, zero solid, no axis lines or ticks, compact value labels, the value title rotated beside its axis, the legend underneath with no title.
table_note: Tables are dense and flat: 8px rows on hairlines, a sunk header in 12px semibold, numbers right-aligned and tabular over a soft turquoise bar scaled to the column. Row hover takes the sunk grey.
card:
Revenue by regionFresh
north$18,400
east$14,350
south$11,220
west$4,240
4 rows · up to 1,000
card_note: A result card: a title and a state tag, then rows whose numbers sit over the quiet bar, and a footer with one outline action and the row count. Hairline, 12px corner, no shadow.

hand.headline: Grey lines, flat colour, nothing raised.
hand.note: Graphite draws like its charts: 1.5px lines in the soft ink with round caps on a white ground, shapes filled flat in the first series at 82%, the second series as a 38% wash under a solid edge. No shadows, no texture; a drawing should look like a chart someone made carefully.
rules: 1.5px in ink-soft, round caps and joins.
Flat: turquoise at 82% for the subject, river blue at 38% for the comparison. Everything else is white.
The sans at 11 to 13px in ink-soft; the one number in the semibold numeral.
None: the drawing is simply there.

motifs_headline: Ink buttons, pills, and a dashed grid.
motifs_note: Graphite's devices come from analytics work: the ink button, the shelf pill, the dashed grid, the kind mark, the quiet bar behind a number, and the status dot with a mode rail. Each keeps colour for data.

motifs.title: The ink button
motifs.usage: The filled button is ink on white (17:1), inverted at night; there is no brand-coloured button. Secondary is white with a hairline, ghost is text that tints on hover. One ink fill per view: the action the screen exists for.

motifs.title: The shelf pill
motifs.usage: A column placed on a shelf: a 32px hairline pill with the column's kind mark, its name, a small tinted select for its grain or aggregation, and a quiet ×. An empty shelf shows a dashed adder in the same size, so filling a shelf never moves the layout.

motifs.title: The dashed grid
motifs.usage: Gridlines run both ways in the hairline, dashed 2 on 4; zero is the one solid line. No axis lines, no ticks, compact value labels (20K, 1.2M), the value title rotated beside its axis and the legend underneath. Bars fill at 82% and stacks part on a hairline of the card colour; areas fill at 38% under a solid edge.

motifs.usage: Every column carries a small mark for what it holds: a clock in turquoise for dates, a hash in river blue for numbers, a letter in carrot for text. The only colour in a list of columns, and the same three everywhere a column appears.

motifs.title: The quiet bar
motifs.usage: In a table every number is right-aligned and tabular, over a soft turquoise bar scaled to its column's largest magnitude. The table reads as a chart without becoming one; text columns stay plain.

motifs.title: The status dot and the mode rail
motifs.usage: State is a 6px dot beside a word; only "running" pulses, in the mark colour. Modes of one screen sit on a slim rail at its left edge: an icon over a short name, the current one on a white tile, never a coloured tab.

dos: Make the primary action an ink fill and everything else outline or ghost.
Keep colour for data, kinds and status; the chrome stays grey and ink.
Draw cards with a hairline on white, never a shadow.
Give charts dashed hairline grids both ways and a solid zero.
Write sentence case everywhere, including shelf labels and column heads.
donts: No brand-coloured buttons, tabs or selected states.
No shadows on cards or tiles; only menus and dialogs float.
No caps, no letter-spaced labels, no bold.
No axis lines, ticks or solid gridlines on charts.
No mark colour as a fill or as body text.
binding_losses: The dashed chart grid, the softened fills, the kind marks, the quiet bar behind numbers and the pressed tile in a mode rail have no contract slot; they are the --ds-grid-dash, --ds-fill-bar, --ds-fill-area and gr-* rules, and a kit chart keeps its own grid unless its spec sets gridDash.
footer: Day first, Night second. Fonts: Instrument Sans 400/500/600 and JetBrains Mono 400/500/600/700, Google-hosted.

tpl.slide_title: Revenue grew 12% with the north region leading.
tpl.slide_sub: North now carries 38% of revenue; west is flat and needs a plan, not more spend.
tpl.slide_body: Existing accounts grew their spend faster than churn removed it. Above 100 is expansion; this quarter it is the highest on record.
tpl.ed_headline: Every chart is one query you can read
tpl.ed_deck: The visual builder no longer hides its work. Each chart shows the SQL it ran, and one click opens it in the editor as a starting point.
tpl.ed_byline: By the data team · 2 Oct 2026 · 3 min read
tpl.ed_body: A chart used to be a black box: you dragged columns around and trusted the picture. Now the shelves compile to a single statement in the connection's own dialect, it runs under the same policy as anything you type, and the statement sits one click under the chart. Copy it, change it, save the result: the picture and the query are the same object.
steps: Each square is one order this quarter, grey until it is placed: 1,284 of them.
The same squares take their region's colour. North is the largest block; west is the smallest and the flattest.
tpl.step_caption: Fig. 1 · Orders this quarter, by region · synthetic
tpl.landing_headline: Ask your data. Read the answer.
tpl.landing_sub: Chart any table by placing columns, or ask in plain words. Every answer is one governed query you can open, check and save.
features: Shelves compile to a single statement in your warehouse's dialect; open it in SQL with one click.
Every query runs as the person asking, under their group's policy. Nothing is unrestricted.
Flat colour only where the data is, on a dashed grid, with the chrome in grey and ink.
tpl.plan_title: Visual explore: from columns to one query
tpl.plan_outcome: A person can place columns on shelves in S1, see the chart and the exact SQL it ran, open that SQL in S2 and save the result, all under their group's policy.
tpl.plan_scope: Shelves (X, Y, Colour, Facet, Filters), the chart (S1), the SQL editor (S2) and the refusal state (S2e). Out: joins across tables, calculated fields, dashboards.
tpl.plan_status: Plan only · 2 of 6 tasks done · compiler verified on both dialects, nothing in production
tpl.plan_screens_note: S1 desktop keeps the column list beside the shelves and the chart; S1 mobile stacks the shelves over the chart and moves the mode rail to a row at the top.
tpl.plan_flow:
flowchart LR
  A((Pick a table)) -->|Place columns| B[S1 Chart]
  B -->|Open in SQL| C{Policy admits?}
  C -->|Yes| D[S2 SQL and rows]
  C -->|No| E[S2e Refused, with the reason]
  E -->|Change the query| C
  D -->|Save result| F((Saved to Artifacts))
plan_decisions: Shelves compile to one statement that runs exactly as typed SQL does, so the picture can always be opened and checked.
Buttons and selection are grey and ink; colour is reserved for series, kinds and status.
A date on X arrives with a last-365-days filter, so a first look never scans a decade.
plan_tasks: Verify every grain against a live warehouse
tpl.plan_acceptance: Done means: a fixture warehouse charts revenue by month and region from S1 in one query, the same SQL opens in S2 and returns the same rows, and a refused table routes to S2e with the reason.
